items.summary: Executive Order 14438, titled "PROTECTING THE EXECUTIVE'S PRIVILEGES AND ENHANCING EFFICIENCIES IN FEDERAL CONTRACTING," dated November 20, 2026, requires all Federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and contracting agencies of pending or future congressional requests concerning their communications or work with the executive branch, and to follow instructions on withholding communications determined to be protected by executive privilege. The order directs the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance on compliance and provides that agencies shall consider contract termination or cancellation and contractor debarment or suspension for noncompliance. It also includes severability and general provisions, states that it creates no enforceable rights, and specifies that publication costs are borne by the Department of Labor.
items.title: PROTECTING THE EXECUTIVE’S PRIVILEGES AND ENHANCING EFFICIENCIES IN FEDERAL CONTRACTING

items.summary: The proclamation titled "NATIONAL ADOPTION MONTH, 2026," dated November 20, 2026, designates November 2026 as National Adoption Month and calls on Americans to ensure that every child has the love and support needed to live a long, healthy, and prosperous life. It references the expanded Adoption Tax Credit, the Fostering the Future Executive Order, the launch of Fostering the Future Accounts, and the FosteringTheFuture.gov website for youth transitioning from foster care. It also encourages faith-based organizations, houses of worship, businesses, nonprofits, and community groups to support adoptive families.
items.title: NATIONAL ADOPTION MONTH, 2026

items.summary: In Byer v. Secretary of Health and Human Services, No. 24-1595V, Special Master Nora Beth Dorsey issued a decision based on stipulation under the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program concerning a petition alleging Guillain-Barré syndrome from an influenza vaccine administered October 13, 2021. The parties' stipulation, filed October 20, 2026, provides a lump sum of $137,911.08 paid by ACH deposit to petitioner's counsel's IOLTA account, and the respondent denies that the vaccine caused the alleged injury. The special master adopted the stipulation as the decision of the court and directed the Clerk of Court to enter judgment absent a motion for review.

items.summary: In Branning v. Secretary of Health and Human Services, No. 25-1788V, Chief Special Master Corcoran issued findings of fact and conclusions of law on October 14, 2026, dismissing the Table shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (SIRVA) claim. The special master found that the petitioner had not established by a preponderance of the evidence that her shoulder pain began within 48 hours of a September 24, 2024 influenza vaccination, relying on contemporaneous records placing onset three to four days after vaccination. The ruling states that an off-Table brachial neuritis claim remains viable and will be transferred out of the Special Processing Unit for resolution.

items.summary: In a published opinion filed November 19, 2026, the Sixth Circuit affirmed a 194-month sentence imposed on Justin Bobo under the Armed Career Criminal Act after he pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The court held that Tennessee robbery remains categorically a violent felony under the ACCA, following its prior decision in United States v. Mitchell, because the Tennessee Supreme Court's decision in State v. Curry addressed only the crime-of-violence element of the unlawful possession statute and did not alter the fear element of robbery defined in State v. Taylor. Accordingly, Bobo's 2010 robbery conviction was held to qualify as a predicate violent felony.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 19, 2026, the Eighth Circuit affirmed a 120-month sentence imposed on Dedric Dewayne Broyles for possession of a firearm by a felon following remand for resentencing. Counsel filed an Anders brief raising two potential issues: whether the district court made the sentence consecutive to an unrelated state-court sentence, and whether the written judgment added a supervised release condition. items.summary: In United States v. Oladapo Sunday Ogunbiyi (3d Cir. No. 25-3300, filed Nov. 19, 2026), a nonprecedential opinion affirmed a 41-month sentence entered by the District of New Jersey after a jury convicted Ogunbiyi of money laundering conspiracy, money laundering, and monetary transaction offenses. items.summary: In a nonprecedential order decided November 19, 2026, the Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for the Village of Lakemoor against former police officer Brianna McCarty on her claims under the ADA and Title VII. The court found that McCarty was not a qualified individual because she could not perform the essential functions of a police officer, and that the Village had offered a reasonable accommodation which she declined. The court also found insufficient evidence to support her sex discrimination and hostile work environment claims.

items.summary: In an opinion decided November 19, 2026, the Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Affiliated FM Insurance Company in a suit by Tower Crossing Condominium Association over storm damage. The court held that the policy's requirement of a 'signed and sworn' proof of loss requires an oath, so a proof of loss that was not sworn did not extend the two-year limitations period. Because the extended period expired before Tower Crossing filed suit, the court concluded the claim was untimely under Illinois law.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–29: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the rules for postponing certain deadlines by reason of disaster. Public Law 29 Public Law 119–29 139 Stat. 471 2025-07-24 2025-07-24 United States Government Publishin
items.summary: Public Law 119–29, cited as the Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act, was approved July 24, 2025. It amends section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to let the Secretary of the Treasury, after consulting the FEMA Administrator and on written request of a State Governor (or the Mayor of the District of Columbia), apply deadline postponement rules to a qualified State-declared disaster, and it defines that term. It also extends the postponement period in that section from 60 days to 120 days, effective for declarations made after the date of enactment.
items.title: Public Law 119–29: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the rules for postponing certain deadlines by reason of disaster.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–72: To amend title 38, United States Code, to modify the conditions under which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs is required to redevelop the individualized vocational rehabilitation plan for a veteran, and for other purpose
items.summary: Public Law 119–72, cited as the FAST VETS Act, was approved January 20, 2026. It amends section 3107(b) of title 38, United States Code, to set conditions under which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs reviews an individualized vocational rehabilitation plan. Under the amended provision, the Secretary may redevelop the plan with a veteran if the long-range rehabilitation goals are no longer feasible due to changes in the veteran's employment handicap and are likelier under a different plan, or may disapprove redevelopment if the Secretary determines it is not appropriate.
items.title: Public Law 119–72: To amend title 38, United States Code, to modify the conditions under which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs is required to redevelop the individualized vocational rehabilitation plan for a veteran, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–87: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes. Public Law 87 Public Law 119–87 140 Stat. 811 2026-04-30 2026-0
items.summary: Public Law 119–87 was approved April 30, 2026, and amends section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. It replaces the April 30, 2026 repeal date in two paragraphs of that section with June 12, 2026. The amendments take effect on the earlier of the date of enactment or April 29, 2026.
items.title: Public Law 119–87: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.

  (Mr. HOYER asked and was given permis
items.summary: Representative Steny Hoyer, speaking in a 60-minute special order as designee of the majority leader, reflected on his 45 years of service and on consensus-building in the House. He described the House passage of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (228-206) on November 5, 2021, and the passage of the Build Back Better Act (220-213) on November 19, 2021. He also cited legislation from the 117th Congress, including the American Rescue Plan, the CHIPS and Science Act, the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, the 2010 repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell, and the 2013 reauthorization of the Export-Import Bank.
items.title: LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP

items.opening_verbatim:
WASHINGTON, D.C., IS A MATH-FREE ZONE

  (Under the Speaker's announced policy of January 3, 2025, Mr.
Schweikert of Arizona was recognized for 60 minutes as the designee of
the majority leader. )
  Mr. SCHWEIKERT. Mr. Spea
items.summary: Representative Schweikert, speaking in a 60-minute special order as designee of the majority leader, discussed daily debt figures published by the Joint Economic Committee, citing total public debt of $40.662 trillion and average borrowing of $78,896 per second over the prior 12 months. The remarks described federal spending categories, stating that mandatory programs account for 76 percent of spending and that 2026 defense spending is $965 billion, and discussed the relationship between marginal tax rates and federal tax receipts as a share of GDP. The Member also stated that OMB and CBO overestimated 2026 revenues.

items.summary: The Senate discharged the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee from H.R. 1520 and passed the bill, as amended by Senator Moody's substitute amendment (No. 7028), under the title 'Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act.' The bill prohibits covered entities from denying organ transplants or related services on the basis of disability and amends section 372(b)(2)(B) of the Public Health Service Act to bar disability-based medical criteria for organ allocation. The bill includes an exception that permits covered entities to consider disability following an individualized assessment in certain circumstances. items.summary: Senator Gillibrand, for Senator Cruz and Senator Rosen, proposed amendment SA 7029 to H.R. 4624, which would strike all after the enacting clause and insert the Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act of 2026. The amendment amends the Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996 to define unified boxing organizations and adds section 21A, which sets requirements including supplemental physical examinations for boxers aged 40 or older, additional ambulances and ringside physicians at covered matches, support services for contracted boxers, and a comprehensive anti-doping program. The amendment also provides for imprisonment of up to one year, a fine of up to $100,000, or both, for officers or employees who knowingly violate section 21A, with the fine increased for matches whose gross revenues exceed $2,000,000.

items.opening_verbatim: IB One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 8454 AN ACT To provide for the transf
items.summary: H.R. 8454 is an enrolled bill from the second session of the 119th Congress that transfers administrative jurisdiction over approximately 160 acres of National Forest System land in Tuolumne County, California, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior, to be managed as part of Yosemite National Park. It also transfers approximately 170 acres of National Park System land in the same county from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of Agriculture, to be managed as part of Stanislaus National Forest, with both transfers referencing the Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange map dated February 24, 2022. The bill permits the two Secretaries, by mutual agreement, to make minor survey and boundary corrections effective upon Federal Register publication, and it preserves valid existing rights and existing withdrawals, rights-of-way, easements, leases, licenses, and permits, which the receiving agency administers under applicable law.
items.title: HR 8454 ENR: To provide for the transfer of administrative jurisdiction over certain Federal land in the State of California, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-4656; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00214-R; Amendment 39-23520; AD 2026-23-03] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deuts
items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, and EC635T2+ helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of a separated tail rotor blade (TRB) assembly due to a crack caused by intergranular corrosion. This AD requires repetitively inspecting a certain TRB assembly for cracks and, depending on the results, removing any cracked TRB assembly from service and replacing an affected part as terminating action for the repetitive inspections. items.summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish ( Cyprinodon tularosa ), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

items.summary: Executive Order 14438, titled "PROTECTING THE EXECUTIVE'S PRIVILEGES AND ENHANCING EFFICIENCIES IN FEDERAL CONTRACTING," dated November 20, 2026, requires all Federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and contracting agencies of pending or future congressional requests concerning their communications or work with the executive branch, and to follow instructions on withholding communications determined to be protected by executive privilege. The order directs the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance on compliance and provides that agencies shall consider contract termination or cancellation and contractor debarment or suspension for noncompliance. It also includes severability and general provisions, states that it creates no enforceable rights, and specifies that publication costs are borne by the Department of Labor.
